body:
Stephanie Nguyen: Need reviewers for the Encryption + KMS one-pager (for the security enablement kit). If you can do a quick pass today/tomorrow, drop comments here so I can track.

Stephanie Nguyen: Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1redwood-g2m-security-kit (doc: “compliance-one-pager-encryption-and-kms”) — aiming to freeze copy by EOD Thu so Design can slot into the new template.

DriveBot: Stephanie Nguyen shared a file: compliance-one-pager-encryption-and-kms-draft

Markus Klein: I can review from SE angle. Main thing I want to make sure we don’t blur Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.

Markus Klein: Also tagging @Marcus Lin @Naomi Feldman @Olga Petrov — this one always gets quoted verbatim in RFPs.

Marcus Lin: Yep I’ll review. Quick initial skim: we should be super explicit on “customer-managed keys” availability. Right now page 1 reads like CMK is universal.

Marcus Lin: Suggest:
- Hosted API: Redwood-managed encryption keys (cloud KMS) + envelope encryption
- Dedicated: options may include customer-managed keys depending on cloud + contract (don’t over-promise “bring your own key” if not always)
- Private: customer controls infra + can integrate with customer KMS/HSM (if supported in that deployment)

Avery Johnson: +1. Customers keep asking “Do you support BYOK?” and “can you use *our* KMS?” — we need that answer clean.

Avery Johnson: Also call out explicitly whether request/response payloads are encrypted at rest anywhere (logs, caches). If the answer is “depends on config / retention,” don’t imply we store everything.

Naomi Feldman: I’m in. Product alignment nit: the “automatic key rotation” line is too strong as written. We should say keys are rotated per our internal policy / cloud provider KMS controls, and for customer-managed keys it’s customer-controlled.

Naomi Feldman: Also the section tying audit logs to KMS (“all key operations are logged”) — careful. We can say we generate audit log events for relevant admin/config actions in Redwood Console; we shouldn’t imply we expose cloud KMS key access logs unless customer owns that layer.

Olga Petrov: Will do GRC pass.

Olga Petrov: Please avoid:
- “ISO 27001 certified” (we are not)
- “HIPAA compliant” / “supports BAA by default” language
- Any statement implying we’ll provide SOC 2 report without NDA

Olga Petrov: Add a standard footnote: “SOC 2 report available under NDA via the evidence request process.”

Camila Reyes: I’ll do messaging/wordsmithing.

Camila Reyes: First edits I’d make:
- Replace “military-grade encryption” (saw this in one sentence) with standard “industry-standard encryption”
- Define acronyms once (KMS, CMK/BYOK)
- Keep “shared responsibility” paragraph short + deployment-mode specific

Fatima Noor: Reviewing for regulated deployments. For Private/VPC audiences, we should include a single sentence that customer can choose region/network boundary and manage keys within their security boundary (where supported) — but don’t claim “air-gapped” unless it’s specifically the on-prem package.

Fatima Noor: Also: spell out the supported integrations at a high level (e.g., AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault / Google Cloud KMS) only if we’re confident. Otherwise say “major cloud KMS providers” and route specifics to SE.

Priyom Das: +1 to being explicit on clouds. Procurement teams will ask “which KMS exactly?”

Priyom Das: If we can’t list them, at least add “availability varies by deployment mode + cloud region” so they don’t assume it’s in Hosted today.

Daniel Carter: Evidence/process nit: add link text (internal) for Sales: “Request SOC 2 / pen test summary via Evidence Request Playbook” and remind: don’t attach reports to emails.

Marcus Lin: Leaving comments in the doc now. High priority edits I’m making:
1) Replace all “BYOK” mentions with “customer-managed keys (where available)” + add deployment-mode table.
2) Clarify: TLS in transit (>=1.2) and encryption at rest (AES-256 via underlying cloud services), but do not specify FIPS.
3) Add a “What we don’t claim” callout: no “FIPS validated” claims in one-pager; if required, escalate.

Elliot Price: I can sanity check the links/CTA at the bottom (docs site vs Confluence vs gated evidence). Please don’t put Confluence URLs in customer-facing PDFs.

Stephanie Nguyen: This is great. Action plan:
- @Marcus Lin: finish technical edits + comment resolution by tomorrow noon
- @Olga Petrov: add GRC-approved footnote language + NDA/evidence request CTA
- @Camila Reyes: rewrite pass for tone/consistency after tech/GRC edits
- @Elliot Price: confirm final outbound links are customer-safe

Stephanie Nguyen: Proposed final approver: Marcus (security) + Olga (GRC). Naomi as FYI for product alignment. If anyone objects, say now.

Naomi Feldman: Works for me. I’ll just re-skim after Marcus updates to make sure the audit log references line up with current docs.

Olga Petrov: Fine by me. Please make sure the final PDF includes “Last reviewed” + version/date.

Marcus Lin: +1. I’ll add “Last reviewed” line and link to the evidence request process (internal) + a customer-friendly “contact your Redwood rep” line for the PDF.

Stephanie Nguyen: Perfect. Deadline: I’ll lock copy at 4pm Thu PT and send to Design (DES-2911 template refresh).
